title: Hilbert-space fragmentation selects channels of strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking
authors: Mingdi Xu, Kaixiang Lu, Daoguang Li, Lei Pan
abstract: Strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SWSSB) can occur in a maximally mixed charge sector even when ordinary charged correlations vanish. We study this order when a charge sector splits into dynamically disconnected fragments. In a one-dimensional $t$-$J_z$ chain with species-resolved dephasing, each fragment is labeled by a conserved spin word. A charged transfer between separated finite intervals preserves that word only if the intervening spins satisfy a periodicity constraint. In the full-state two-point sense, we use this constraint to prove the absence of long-range fidelity and Rényi-1 order in typical fixed-composition fragments, uniformly over all norm-bounded charged operators in any prescribed finite interval. A fragment with primitive spin-word period $k$ supports a $k$-particle channel with exact long-distance value $ν^k(1-ν)^k/k^2$, and no charged operator on fewer than $k$ sites can carry this order. A transverse exchange connects the fragments while preserving the global charges and restores the full-sector steady state at finite size. The conserved spin word therefore selects the local channels that can support mixed-state order.
summary: This paper analyzes spontaneous symmetry breaking in a dephasing quantum chain where the Hilbert space fragments. By using nonlinear correlation functions, the authors prove that most fragments lose long-range order, while only specific channels dictated by the periodicity of the conserved 'spin word' can sustain residual order. This highlights how local constraints can select specific, robust physical channels even when global order is lost.
main_problem: The study investigates Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking (SWSSB) in quantum systems whose Hilbert space fragments into dynamically disconnected subspaces beyond simple global charge conservation.
main_result: The analysis shows that while the full system can retain long-range order via transverse exchange, typical, isolated fragments fail to support conventional two-point nonlinear order, except for specific channels dictated by the fragment's underlying spin-word periodicity.
method: The authors use nonlinear correlators, specifically fidelity and Rényi-1 order, to diagnose symmetry breaking, comparing results derived from the full-state dynamics versus those restricted to individual word fragments.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional t-Jz chain subjected to species-resolved dephasing, governed by a Lindblad master equation. The dynamics are analyzed based on the conservation of a 'spin word' when the system fragments.
key_observables: Fidelity ($F_O$), Rényi-1 correlators ($R_{1,O}$), and the Rényi-2 diagnostic ($g_2(t)$) are used to quantify the degree of spontaneous symmetry breaking and long-range order.
important_parameters: The key parameters include the periodicity ($k$) of the conserved spin word, the gap size ($r$), and the coupling strength $J_\perp$ which connects the fragments.
main_assumptions: The analysis distinguishes between the order supported by the full sector (global charge) and the order supported by individual, fixed-composition word fragments.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the spin-word fragmentation pattern, compare the suppression of local nonlinear order in typical fragments versus the full sector, and show how transverse exchange restores sector correlations.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the physical model and the concept of word fragmentation, then using nonlinear correlators to prove the absence of order in typical fragments, and finally identifying the specific, periodic channels that can support residual order.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated diagnostic tool (nonlinear correlators) to probe subtle forms of symmetry breaking in non-equilibrium, open quantum systems, linking microscopic constraints (spin words) to macroscopic order parameters.
